Visualizing differential neighborhood-enrichment networks

CellCharterR contributors

2026-10-15

1 Purpose

Differential neighborhood enrichment asks whether a directed domain-to-domain neighborhood association is stronger in one biological condition than another. This vignette uses the completed full mouse-spleen analysis with the independently selected K = 4 solution. It demonstrates visualization only: the graph, clustering, neighborhood statistics, and permutations are not recomputed while building this vignette.

The stored contrast is BALBc minus MRL. Rows of each matrix represent the source or central domain, columns represent the surrounding or neighboring domain, and arrows therefore point source -> neighbor. Positive effects are shown in the BALBc panel; negative effects are displayed by absolute magnitude in the MRL panel. Both panels reuse the same permutation p-values.

2 Load the completed result

library(CellCharterR)

k4_result <- readRDS(system.file(
  "extdata",
  "mouse_spleen_k4_diff_nhood.rds",
  package = "CellCharterR"
))

k4_enrichment <- readRDS(system.file(
  "extdata",
  "mouse_spleen_k4_enrichment.rds",
  package = "CellCharterR"
))

k4_result$params[c(
  "contrast_definition", "library_unit", "library_counts",
  "n_perms", "permutation_mode", "empirical_tail"
)]

This result compares three BALBc libraries with six MRL libraries, uses the sample as the permutation unit, and contains 100 permutations with the pinned CellCharter 0.2.0 compatibility mode. Its SHA-256 checksum is ae65446954faeb1b15aa53bcf5f1ec45e2ebd09d553a61a12c59c28029c3f6d7. The matching cell-type enrichment artifact has SHA-256 checksum be78548f33e16fd2f668c79cd7aa539a97df95f4a9a7ccdd0ab1b00665c0d261.

3 Meet the ecosystems

Before interpreting connections between domains, first inspect which cell types characterize each domain. The dot plot shows positive observed-to-expected cell-type enrichment as log2 fold change. Darker and larger red points indicate stronger positive enrichment; non-positive values remain in the stored result but are omitted from this display, following the CellCharter presentation.

cellcharter_plot_enrichment(
  k4_enrichment,
  title = "Cell types defining the K=4 spatial ecosystems"
)

Figure 1: Cell-type enrichment defining the four K=4 mouse-spleen spatial ecosystems

These enrichment profiles provide the biological context for the numbered nodes below: each network node is one of these four spatial ecosystems, not an individual cell type.

4 Inspect both differential contrasts

Before reducing the result to arrows, inspect the complete directed effect matrices. The stored effect is BALBc minus MRL; the reciprocal display negates that effect while retaining the same directional empirical p-values. Rows are source ecosystems and columns are neighboring target ecosystems. A star marks an empirical p <= 0.05 from the 100 sample-level permutations.

contrast_long <- function(effect, pvalue, contrast) {
  value <- as.data.frame(as.table(effect), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  names(value) <- c("source", "target", "effect")
  value$pvalue <- as.vector(pvalue)
  value$contrast <- contrast
  value$label <- ifelse(
    is.finite(value$effect),
    paste0(sprintf("%.2f", value$effect), ifelse(value$pvalue <= 0.05, " *", "")),
    ""
  )
  value
}

contrast_heatmaps <- rbind(
  contrast_long(k4_result$effect, k4_result$pvalue, "BALBc minus MRL"),
  contrast_long(-k4_result$effect, k4_result$pvalue, "MRL minus BALBc")
)
effect_limit <- max(abs(contrast_heatmaps$effect), na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot2::ggplot(
  contrast_heatmaps,
  ggplot2::aes(x = target, y = source, fill = effect)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = label), size = 5) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~contrast, nrow = 1) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#8B0000",
    midpoint = 0, limits = c(-effect_limit, effect_limit),
    name = "Differential\nenrichment"
  ) +
  ggplot2::coord_fixed() +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Neighboring ecosystem (target)",
    y = "Central ecosystem (source)"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_bw(base_size = 16) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold")
  )

Figure 2: Full K=4 differential neighborhood-enrichment matrices in both display directions

These heatmaps retain every directed off-diagonal comparison, including weak or unsupported effects. The network views below summarize the same matrices; they do not perform a second statistical test.

5 Plot both favored-condition networks

Black arrows are the default. Solid arrows pass the displayed statistical threshold; dashed arrows are retained effects that are not statistically supported at that threshold. Arrow width is intentionally constant, so it does not create an additional visual claim about magnitude.

cellcharter_plot_graph_diff(k4_result)

Figure 3: Full mouse-spleen K=4 differential neighborhood-enrichment network
The two panels share identical node coordinates.

The graph is asymmetric: domain 0 -> domain 2 and domain 2 -> domain 0 are different directed hypotheses. Their effects and p-values must not be combined or interpreted as an undirected connection.

6 Apply user-defined condition colors

Colors are presentation choices, not part of the statistical test. A single color applies to both panels; a named vector can assign one color per condition.

cellcharter_plot_graph_diff(
  k4_result,
  edge_colours = c(BALBc = "#2166AC", MRL = "#B2182B"),
  top_n = 4
)

Figure 4: The same result with user-supplied condition colors and the strongest four arrows retained independently per panel

top_n is a display filter. It is applied independently in each panel after p-values have been evaluated and therefore does not alter the p-values or their multiple-testing adjustment.

7 Focus on statistically supported arrows

The reference-compatible default uses raw directional empirical p-values. For exploratory multiplicity control, select a method supported by stats::p.adjust(); adjustment is performed across every eligible directed off-diagonal hypothesis before display filtering.

cellcharter_plot_graph_diff(
  k4_result,
  significant_only = TRUE,
  alpha = 0.05
)

Figure 5: Edges supported by the raw directional empirical p-value threshold of 0.05

8 Illustrative interpretation

In this K = 4 result, the largest positive displayed effect is the directed association from domain 1 to domain 2, favoring BALBc. At the raw threshold of 0.05, three BALBc-favored arrows are retained and no MRL-favored arrow passes the same threshold. A recorded p-value of zero means that none of the 100 reference-compatible permutation draws was as extreme; it does not mean that the probability is literally zero.

These domain numbers do not themselves identify cell types or mechanisms. Biological interpretation should combine this network with the corresponding spatial maps, cell-type enrichment results, sample-level consistency, and the known limitations of the K = 4 domain resolution. The figure is therefore a diagnostic summary of the computed differential neighborhood result, not proof of a causal interaction.

9 Reproduce the expensive analysis

The following code documents where the plotted result originates, but it is not run when the vignette is built.

full_spe <- cellcharter_diff_nhood_enrichment(
  full_spe,
  graph_name = "cellcharter_graph",
  domain_col = "cellcharter_domain_k4",
  condition_col = "condition",
  sample_col = "sample",
  condition_groups = c("BALBc", "MRL"),
  n_perms = 100L,
  seed = 0L,
  permutation_mode = "cellcharter_v0.2.0"
)

cellcharter_plot_graph_diff(full_spe)
